End-of-Support OS on Customer SFTP File.reason: The SFTP servers run an operating system that reached end of support in January 2026 and no longer gets security patches, while broad /16 allowlist ranges add a smaller misconfiguration issue.

No MFA on Legacy Support Admin Console.reason: The legacy support admin console uses username and password only and is not integrated with SSO, so multi-factor authentication is absent for accounts with tenant impersonation privilege.

Over-Privileged CI/CD Deployment Role in.reason: The CI/CD deployment role exists but is set up with wildcard administrative permissions and long-lived keys instead of least-privilege scoped access, with stale key rotation and a long-unresolved posture finding as secondary process issues.

User Access Reviews Not Performed for Pa.reason: Quarterly access reviews were skipped for two quarters because the application owner role was vacant, and the 30 local accounts fall outside the SSO-based leaver process.

Unsupported Insecure Protocol on Third-P.reason: The integration runs on a legacy SOAP API version the provider no longer supports and issues no security fixes for, which is also a supplier-side dependency, with TLS 1.0 and a shared basic-auth account adding weak settings.

No Data Loss Prevention on Workstations.reason: The workstations have no DLP agent or egress monitoring and do not block USB or personal cloud storage, while extracts are also left untracked with no retention limit enforced.

Backup Restoration Untested for Time and.reason: Backups run nightly but no full restore test has been performed in 19 months, including after a major schema change and storage migration, so recoverability against the 8-hour objective is unverified.

Hardcoded Secrets in Source Code Reposit.reason: There is no pre-commit or push-time secret scanning, so 212 hardcoded secrets sit in repositories, while voluntary vault use and unrotated secrets also point to a process gap.

Overdue Security Assessment for Support.reason: The vendor's security assessment is 14 months overdue, its SOC 2 report is stale, and written confirmation of a sub-processor incident is missing, so the weakness lies in supplier oversight and in customer PII held by the vendor.
